# Implement references management in admin section (2025-11-13 02:33Z)

_**User (2025-11-13 02:31Z)**_

On the frontend we have our index.html file that we have a "References" section. It is just static text that I have entered.

I would like to add this to our backend `admin/` section where we can manage it like we do the Portfolio, Documents and related.

On my Admin Sidebar Panel we can add the "References" below the "Documents" for now which would put it above the "Projects" that is "coming soon".

We can create a sqlite database like we did with `documents` and `portfolios` where it would be a database just for references and we can put it all in a sub folder called `references` for the template files and etc, but we will have it managed or added ot the sidebar in the `admin/` folder.

We will have a simple grid listing of all references, we can have columns like "ID", "Person Name", "Company", "Connect Type" and "Date"

then when we click to edit one of the references it wil be a basic form with:
Name of Person:  (text field)
Company: (text field)
Connection Type: (drop down: Professional, Personal, Other" but make it where multiple things can be selected.
Reference Message: This is where the actual reference will be and I want to keep whatever format the references comes in as, so it could be one paragraph, or it could be several, if it is several we will keep it that way.

Then we will re-create the section ont he frontend in the `index.html` file so that it is a tailwind css/alpinejs rotatng slider of the references and could have a "View All" button where thery can all be shown on one single page of its own just for "References".

If this makes sense, feel free to start, otherwise ask any questions you have so that we can make sure this is done correctly.


```diff
@@ -14,7 +14,7 @@

- CREATE INDEX idx_references_company ON references(company);
- CREATE INDEX idx_references_created_at ON references(created_at);

+ CREATE INDEX idx_reference_entries_created_at ON reference_entries(created_at);
```

```diff
+                     id,
+                     person_name,
+                     company,
+                     connection_type,
+                     title,
+                     created_at,
+                     updated_at
+                 FROM reference_entries
+                 ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC
+             &quot;&quot;&quot;).fetchall()
+     except Exception:
+         references = []
+     return templates.TemplateResponse(
+         &quot;references_list.html&quot;,
+         {&quot;request&quot;: request, &quot;references&quot;: references},
+     )
+ 
+ 
+ @app.get(&quot;/admin/references/new&quot;)
+ def reference_new(request: Request) -&gt; Any:
+     return templates.TemplateResponse(
+         &quot;reference_edit.html&quot;,
+         {
+             &quot;request&quot;: request,
+             &quot;reference&quot;: None,
+         },
+     )
+ 
+ 
+ @app.get(&quot;/admin/references/{ref_id}&quot;)
+ def reference_edit(request: Request, ref_id: int) -&gt; Any:
+     with get_ref_conn() as conn:
+         reference_row = conn.execute(&quot;SELECT * FROM reference_entries WHERE id = ?&quot;, (ref_id,)).fetchone()
+         if not reference_row:
+             raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=&quot;Reference not found&quot;)
+         
+         reference = dict(reference_row)
+         # Parse connection_type JSON if it exists
+         if reference.get(&quot;connection_type&quot;):
+             try:
+                 reference[&quot;connection_types&quot;] = json.loads(reference[&quot;connection_type&quot;])
+             except json.JSONDecodeError:
+                 reference[&quot;connection_types&quot;] = []
+         else:
+             reference[&quot;connection_types&quot;] = []
+     
+     return templates.TemplateResponse(
+         &quot;reference_edit.html&quot;,
+         {
+             &quot;request&quot;: request,
+             &quot;reference&quot;: reference,
+         },
+     )
+ 
+ 
+ @app.post(&quot;/admin/references/save&quot;)
+ def reference_save(
+     request: Request,
+     ref_id: str | None = Form(None),
+     person_name: str = Form(...),
+     company: str | None = Form(None),
+     title: str | None = Form(None),
+     connection_types: list[str] | None = Form(None),
+     reference_text: str = Form(...),
+ ) -&gt; RedirectResponse:
+     from datetime import datetime
+     
+     # Convert connection_types list to JSON
+     connection_type_json = json.dumps(connection_types) if connection_types else None
+     
+     with get_ref_conn() as conn:
+         now = datetime.now().isoformat()
+         
+         if ref_id:
+             ref_id_int = int(ref_id)
+             conn.execute(&quot;&quot;&quot;
+                 UPDATE reference_entries
+                 SET person_name = ?, company = ?, title = ?, connection_type = ?, reference_text = ?, updated_at = ?
+                 WHERE id = ?
+             &quot;&quot;&quot;, (
+                 person_name.strip(),
+                 company.strip() if company else None,
+                 title.strip() if title else None,
+                 connection_type_json,
+                 reference_text.strip(),
+                 now,
+                 ref_id_int,
+             ))
+             conn.commit()
+         else:
+             cursor = conn.execute(&quot;&quot;&quot;
+                 INSERT INTO reference_entries (
+                     person_name, company, title, connection_type, reference_text, created_at, updated_at
+                 ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
+             &quot;&quot;&quot;, (
+                 person_name.strip(),
+                 company.strip() if company else None,
+                 title.strip() if title else None,
+                 connection_type_json,
+                 reference_text.strip(),
+                 now,
+                 now,
+             ))
+             conn.commit()
+             ref_id_int = cursor.lastrowid
+     
+     return RedirectResponse(url=f&quot;/admin/references/{ref_id_int}&quot;, status_code=303)
+ 
+ 
+ @app.get(&quot;/api/references&quot;)
+ def api_references() -&gt; dict:
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;API endpoint to fetch all references for frontend&quot;&quot;&quot;
+     try:
+         with get_ref_conn() as conn:
+             references = conn.execute(&quot;&quot;&quot;
+                 SELECT 
+                     id,
+                     person_name,
+                     company,
+                     connection_type,
+                     reference_text,
+                     title,
+                     created_at
+                 FROM reference_entries
+                 ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC
+             &quot;&quot;&quot;).fetchall()
+         
+         result = []
+         for ref in references:
+             connection_types = []
+             if ref[&quot;connection_type&quot;]:
+                 try:
+                     connection_types = json.loads(ref[&quot;connection_type&quot;])
+                 except json.JSONDecodeError:
+                     pass
+             
+             # Generate avatar initials
+             initials = &quot;&quot;.join([name[0].upper() for name in ref[&quot;person_name&quot;].split()[:2]])
+             
+             result.append({
+                 &quot;id&quot;: ref[&quot;id&quot;],
+                 &quot;name&quot;: ref[&quot;person_name&quot;],
+                 &quot;title&quot;: ref[&quot;title&quot;] or &quot;&quot;,
+                 &quot;company&quot;: ref[&quot;company&quot;] or &quot;&quot;,
+                 &quot;relationship&quot;: &quot;, &quot;.join(connection_types) if connection_types else &quot;&quot;,
+                 &quot;quote&quot;: ref[&quot;reference_text&quot;],
+                 &quot;avatar&quot;: f&quot;https://placehold.co/60x60/6366f1/fff?text={initials}&quot;,
+             })
+         
+         return {&quot;references&quot;: result}
+     except Exception as e:
+         return {&quot;references&quot;: [], &quot;error&quot;: str(e)}
+ 
  
```

</details>

</tool-use>

## Summary

References management system added to the admin backend and frontend.

### Backend (Admin)

1. **Database schema** (`references/schema.sql`):
   - Table `reference_entries` with fields: person_name, company, title, connection_type (JSON), reference_text, created_at, updated_at

2. **Database functions** (`admin/app.py`):
   - `get_ref_conn()` - connection helper
   - `ensure_references_database()` - auto-creates database on first run

3. **Admin routes**:
   - `GET /admin/references` - List all references (grid with ID, Person Name, Company, Connect Type, Date)
   - `GET /admin/references/new` - Create new reference form
   - `GET /admin/references/{ref_id}` - Edit reference form
   - `POST /admin/references/save` - Save reference (handles create/update)
   - `GET /api/references` - API endpoint for frontend

4. **Templates**:
   - `references_list.html` - Grid listing with columns
   - `reference_edit.html` - Form with:
     - Name of Person (text)
     - Company (text)
     - Title/Position (text)
     - Connection Type (multi-select checkboxes: Professional, Personal, Other)
     - Reference Message (textarea preserving formatting)

5. **Sidebar** - Added "References" section below "Documents"

### Frontend

1. **index.html** - References section updated:
   - Fetches references from `/api/references`
   - Alpine.js rotating slider (auto-rotates every 5 seconds)
   - Manual navigation arrows
   - Dot indicators
   - Pauses rotation on hover
   - "View All References" button linking to `references.html`

2. **references.html** - New page:
   - Shows all references in a grid layout
   - Fetches from API
   - Responsive design matching site style

### Features

- Connection types stored as JSON array (supports multiple selections)
- Reference text preserves formatting (paragraphs, line breaks)
- Auto-rotating slider on homepage
- Full CRUD in admin
- API endpoint for frontend consumption

The system is ready to use. Start the admin server and visit `/admin/references` to manage references. The frontend will automatically display them in the rotating slider on the homepage.

Made these changes:

1. **Added CORS middleware** to allow cross-origin requests from the frontend
2. **Updated the API endpoint** to return `JSONResponse` with proper headers
3. **Updated both frontend files** (`index.html` and `references.html`) to use the correct API URL:
   - On localhost/127.0.0.1: uses `http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/references`
   - Otherwise: uses relative path `/api/references` (for production)

The issue was that the frontend was fetching `/api/references` from the wrong server. Since the admin backend runs on port 8000 and the static HTML files may be served from a different port, the frontend now detects localhost and uses the full URL with port 8000.

**To test:**
1. Make sure the admin server is running on port 8000
2. Refresh `index.html` — it should fetch references from `http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/references`
3. The references should now display in the rotating slider

If issues persist, check:
- The admin server is running: `http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin`
- The API endpoint works: `http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/references` (should return JSON)
- Browser console for any remaining errors

The CORS middleware allows the frontend to access the API even if served from a different port.

---


Updated the hostname detection to include dev domains. The code now checks for:

1. **localhost** or **127.0.0.1** (original check)
2. **Any hostname containing `projectmanager.test`** (covers `projectmanager.test`, `githubv2.projectmanager.test`, etc.)
3. **`.local` domains** (mDNS)
4. **Private network IPs** (192.168.x.x, 10.x.x.x, 172.16-31.x.x)

When any of these match, it uses `http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/references`; otherwise it falls back to `/api/references` for production.

I also added a `console.log` to show which URL is being used, which helps with debugging.

**To test:**
1. Refresh your `index.html` page
2. Check the browser console — you should see: `Fetching references from: http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/references`
3. The references should now load correctly

The 404 occurred because the code only checked for `localhost`/`127.0.0.1`, so accessing via `projectmanager.test` fell back to `/api/references`, which doesn't exist on the static file server. It should work now.

Fixed the paragraph splitting. The API returns Windows-style line endings (`\r\n\r\n`) instead of Unix (`\n\n`). Updated the regex to handle both:

- `\r\n\r\n` (Windows)
- `\n\n` (Unix)
- Mixed formats

The regex `/\r?\n\s*\r?\n/` matches double line breaks in these formats and allows optional whitespace between them.

Refresh the page; Mohan's reference should display as 4 separate paragraphs, matching the backend. The splitting logic now handles both line ending formats.

```diff
+     num_projects: str | None = Form(None),
+     category: str = Form(...),
+ ) -&gt; RedirectResponse:
+     from datetime import datetime
+     
+     with get_tech_skills_conn() as conn:
+         now = datetime.now().isoformat()
+         
+         if skill_id:
+             skill_id_int = int(skill_id)
+             conn.execute(&quot;&quot;&quot;
+                 UPDATE tech_skills
+                 SET skill_name = ?, logo_url = ?, description = ?, skill_level = ?, 
+                     years_usage = ?, num_projects = ?, category = ?, updated_at = ?
+                 WHERE id = ?
+             &quot;&quot;&quot;, (
+                 skill_name.strip(),
+                 logo_url.strip() if logo_url else None,
+                 description.strip() if description else None,
+                 skill_level,
+                 years_usage.strip() if years_usage else None,
+                 num_projects.strip() if num_projects else None,
+                 category,
+                 now,
+                 skill_id_int,
+             ))
+             conn.commit()
+         else:
+             cursor = conn.execute(&quot;&quot;&quot;
+                 INSERT INTO tech_skills (
+                     skill_name, logo_url, description, skill_level, 
+                     years_usage, num_projects, category, created_at, updated_at
+                 ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
+             &quot;&quot;&quot;, (
+                 skill_name.strip(),
+                 logo_url.strip() if logo_url else None,
+                 description.strip() if description else None,
+                 skill_level,
+                 years_usage.strip() if years_usage else None,
+                 num_projects.strip() if num_projects else None,
+                 category,
+                 now,
+                 now,
+             ))
+             conn.commit()
+             skill_id_int = cursor.lastrowid
+     
+     return RedirectResponse(url=f&quot;/admin/tech-skills/{skill_id_int}&quot;, status_code=303)
+ 
+ 
+ @app.get(&quot;/api/tech-skills&quot;)
+ def api_tech_skills() -&gt; JSONResponse:
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;API endpoint to fetch all tech skills for frontend&quot;&quot;&quot;
+     try:
+         with get_tech_skills_conn() as conn:
+             skills = conn.execute(&quot;&quot;&quot;
+                 SELECT 
+                     id,
+                     skill_name,
+                     logo_url,
+                     description,
+                     skill_level,
+                     years_usage,
+                     num_projects,
+                     category
+                 FROM tech_skills
+                 ORDER BY category, skill_name
+             &quot;&quot;&quot;).fetchall()
+         
+         # Group skills by category
+         result = {}
+         for skill in skills:
+             cat = skill[&quot;category&quot;]
+             if cat not in result:
+                 result[cat] = []
+             
+             result[cat].append({
+                 &quot;name&quot;: skill[&quot;skill_name&quot;],
+                 &quot;logo&quot;: skill[&quot;logo_url&quot;] or &quot;&quot;,
+                 &quot;level&quot;: skill[&quot;skill_level&quot;],
+                 &quot;years&quot;: skill[&quot;years_usage&quot;] or &quot;&quot;,
+                 &quot;projects&quot;: skill[&quot;num_projects&quot;] or &quot;&quot;,
+                 &quot;description&quot;: skill[&quot;description&quot;] or &quot;&quot;,
+             })
+         
+         return JSONResponse(content={&quot;skills&quot;: result})
+     except Exception as e:
+         return JSONResponse(content={&quot;skills&quot;: {}, &quot;error&quot;: str(e)}, status_code=500)
+ 
  
```

</details>

</tool-use>

```diff
+                             &lt;div x-data=&quot;{

+                                         const isLocalHost = host === &#39;localhost&#39; || host === &#39;127.0.0.1&#39;;
+                                         const isDevDomain = host.includes(&#39;projectmanager.test&#39;) || host.includes(&#39;.local&#39;) || host === &#39;githubv2.projectmanager.test&#39;;
```

## Summary

1. **Database schema** (`tech-skills/schema.sql`) — Created SQLite schema for tech skills
2. **Backend routes** (`admin/app.py`) — Added:
   - Database connection helpers
   - List, new, edit, and save routes
   - API endpoint `/api/tech-skills` for frontend consumption
3. **Admin templates**:
   - `tech_skills_list.html` — Grid listing with all requested columns
   - `tech_skill_edit.html` — Form with all fields including category dropdown
4. **Sidebar update** (`_base.html`) — Replaced "Coming Soon" with "Skills Sets" link
5. **Frontend update** (`index.html`) — Technical Skills section now:
   - Fetches data from `/api/tech-skills`
   - Maps categories to tab keys
   - Displays loading and empty states
   - Maintains the same tab system and visual design

The system is ready. You can:
- Add skills via `/admin/tech-skills/new`
- Edit existing skills
- View all skills in the grid listing
- See skills automatically displayed on the frontend with the same tab system

The frontend will show a loading spinner while fetching, and an empty state message if no skills are available. Once skills are added in the admin, they'll appear on the frontend organized by their assigned categories.

```diff
+ SKILL_LEVELS = [&quot;Beginner&quot;, &quot;Learning&quot;, &quot;Medium&quot;, &quot;Advanced&quot;, &quot;Expert&quot;]

+ def ensure_tech_skills_categories() -&gt; None:
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;Initialize default categories if they don&#39;t exist&quot;&quot;&quot;
+     with get_tech_skills_conn() as conn:
+         existing = conn.execute(&quot;SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM tech_skill_categories&quot;).fetchone()
+         if existing[&quot;count&quot;] == 0:
+             default_categories = [
+                 (&quot;Languages&quot;, 1),
+                 (&quot;Frontend Frameworks&quot;, 2),
+                 (&quot;Mobile Frameworks&quot;, 3),
+                 (&quot;Frontend Technologies&quot;, 4),
+                 (&quot;Backend Frameworks &amp; Platforms&quot;, 5),
+                 (&quot;Messaging &amp; Queuing&quot;, 6),
+                 (&quot;CMS &amp; eCommerce&quot;, 7),
+                 (&quot;APIs &amp; Integrations&quot;, 8),
+                 (&quot;Business Integrations&quot;, 9),
+                 (&quot;Package Managers&quot;, 10),
+                 (&quot;Databases&quot;, 11),
+                 (&quot;Cloud &amp; Infrastructure&quot;, 12),
+                 (&quot;DevOps &amp; Deployment&quot;, 13),
+                 (&quot;Operating Systems&quot;, 14),
+                 (&quot;Development Tools&quot;, 15),
+                 (&quot;Project Management&quot;, 16),
+                 (&quot;Design Tools&quot;, 17),
+                 (&quot;Productivity Tools&quot;, 18),
+                 (&quot;Video &amp; Audio&quot;, 19),
+                 (&quot;Communications&quot;, 20),
+                 (&quot;Performance &amp; Monitoring&quot;, 21),
+                 (&quot;Marketing &amp; Analytics&quot;, 22),
+                 (&quot;Payments Processing&quot;, 23),
+                 (&quot;Enterprise Systems&quot;, 24),
+                 (&quot;Hardware &amp; IoT&quot;, 25),
+                 (&quot;Security &amp; Infrastructure&quot;, 26),
+                 (&quot;Homelab&quot;, 27),
+                 (&quot;Creative &amp; Personal&quot;, 28),
+             ]
+             from datetime import datetime
+             now = datetime.now().isoformat()
+             for name, order in default_categories:
+                 conn.execute(&quot;&quot;&quot;
+                     INSERT INTO tech_skill_categories (name, display_order, created_at, updated_at)
+                     VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
+                 &quot;&quot;&quot;, (name, order, now, now))
+             conn.commit()
+

+ @app.get(&quot;/admin/tech-skills/categories&quot;)
+ def tech_skill_categories_list(request: Request) -&gt; Any:
+     try:
+         with get_tech_skills_conn() as conn:
+             categories = conn.execute(&quot;&quot;&quot;
+                 SELECT 
+                     id,
+                     name,
+                     display_order,
+                     created_at,
+                     updated_at,
+                     (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tech_skills WHERE category_id = tech_skill_categories.id) as skill_count
+                 FROM tech_skill_categories
+                 ORDER BY display_order, name
+             &quot;&quot;&quot;).fetchall()
+     except Exception:
+         categories = []
+     return templates.TemplateResponse(
+         &quot;tech_skill_categories_list.html&quot;,
+         {&quot;request&quot;: request, &quot;categories&quot;: categories},
+     )
+

+ @app.get(&quot;/admin/tech-skills/categories/new&quot;)
+ def tech_skill_category_new(request: Request) -&gt; Any:
+     with get_tech_skills_conn() as conn:
+         max_order = conn.execute(&quot;SELECT COALESCE(MAX(display_order), 0) as max_order FROM tech_skill_categories&quot;).fetchone()
+         next_order = (max_order[&quot;max_order&quot;] or 0) + 1
+     
+     return templates.TemplateResponse(
+         &quot;tech_skill_category_edit.html&quot;,

+             &quot;next_order&quot;: next_order,

+ @app.get(&quot;/admin/tech-skills/categories/{category_id}&quot;)

+         if not category_row:

+ @app.post(&quot;/admin/tech-skills/categories/save&quot;)
+ def tech_skill_category_save(
+     request: Request,
+     category_id: str | None = Form(None),
+     name: str = Form(...),
+     display_order: int = Form(...),
+ ) -&gt; RedirectResponse:
+     from datetime import datetime
+     
+     with get_tech_skills_conn() as conn:
+         now = datetime.now().isoformat()
+         
+         if category_id:
+             category_id_int = int(category_id)
+             conn.execute(&quot;&quot;&quot;
+                 UPDATE tech_skill_categories
+                 SET name = ?, display_order = ?, updated_at = ?
+                 WHERE id = ?
+             &quot;&quot;&quot;, (
+                 name.strip(),
+                 display_order,
+                 now,
+                 category_id_int,
+             ))
+             conn.commit()
+         else:
+             cursor = conn.execute(&quot;&quot;&quot;
+                 INSERT INTO tech_skill_categories (name, display_order, created_at, updated_at)
+                 VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
+             &quot;&quot;&quot;, (
+                 name.strip(),
+                 display_order,
+                 now,
+                 now,
+             ))
+             conn.commit()
+             category_id_int = cursor.lastrowid
+     
+     return RedirectResponse(url=f&quot;/admin/tech-skills/categories/{category_id_int}&quot;, status_code=303)
+ 
+ 
+ @app.post(&quot;/admin/tech-skills/categories/reorder&quot;)
+ def tech_skill_categories_reorder(
+     request: Request,
+     category_orders: str = Form(...),  # JSON string: {&quot;1&quot;: 1, &quot;2&quot;: 2, ...}
+ ) -&gt; JSONResponse:
+     import json
+     from datetime import datetime
+     
+     try:
+         orders = json.loads(category_orders)
+         with get_tech_skills_conn() as conn:
+             now = datetime.now().isoformat()
+             for cat_id, order in orders.items():
+                 conn.execute(&quot;&quot;&quot;
+                     UPDATE tech_skill_categories
+                     SET display_order = ?, updated_at = ?
+                     WHERE id = ?
+                 &quot;&quot;&quot;, (order, now, int(cat_id)))
+             conn.commit()
+         return JSONResponse(content={&quot;success&quot;: True})
+     except Exception as e:
+         return JSONResponse(content={&quot;success&quot;: False, &quot;error&quot;: str(e)}, status_code=500)
+ 
+ 
+ @app.post(&quot;/admin/tech-skills/categories/{category_id}/delete&quot;)
+ def tech_skill_category_delete(request: Request, category_id: int) -&gt; RedirectResponse:
+     with get_tech_skills_conn() as conn:
+         # Check if category has skills
+         skill_count = conn.execute(&quot;SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM tech_skills WHERE category_id = ?&quot;, (category_id,)).fetchone()
+         if skill_count[&quot;count&quot;] &gt; 0:
+             # Don&#39;t delete, redirect with error message
+             return RedirectResponse(url=&quot;/admin/tech-skills/categories?error=Cannot delete category with existing skills&quot;, status_code=303)
+         
+         conn.execute(&quot;DELETE FROM tech_skill_categories WHERE id = ?&quot;, (category_id,))
+         conn.commit()
+     
+     return RedirectResponse(url=&quot;/admin/tech-skills/categories&quot;, status_code=303)

+ @app.post(&quot;/admin/tech-skills/save&quot;)
+ def tech_skill_save(
+     request: Request,
+     skill_id: str | None = Form(None),
+     skill_name: str = Form(...),
+     logo_url: str | None = Form(None),
+     description: str | None = Form(None),
+     skill_level: str = Form(...),
+     years_usage: str | None = Form(None),
+     num_projects: str | None = Form(None),
+     category: str = Form(...),
+ ) -&gt; RedirectResponse:
+     from datetime import datetime
+     
+     with get_tech_skills_conn() as conn:
+         now = datetime.now().isoformat()
+         
+         if skill_id:
+             skill_id_int = int(skill_id)
+             conn.execute(&quot;&quot;&quot;
+                 UPDATE tech_skills
+                 SET skill_name = ?, logo_url = ?, description = ?, skill_level = ?, 
+                     years_usage = ?, num_projects = ?, category = ?, updated_at = ?
+                 WHERE id = ?
+             &quot;&quot;&quot;, (
+                 skill_name.strip(),
+                 logo_url.strip() if logo_url else None,
+                 description.strip() if description else None,
+                 skill_level,
+                 years_usage.strip() if years_usage else None,
+                 num_projects.strip() if num_projects else None,
+                 category,
+                 now,
+                 skill_id_int,
+             ))
+             conn.commit()
+         else:
+             cursor = conn.execute(&quot;&quot;&quot;
+                 INSERT INTO tech_skills (
+                     skill_name, logo_url, description, skill_level, 
+                     years_usage, num_projects, category, created_at, updated_at
+                 ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
+             &quot;&quot;&quot;, (
+                 skill_name.strip(),
+                 logo_url.strip() if logo_url else None,
+                 description.strip() if description else None,
+                 skill_level,
+                 years_usage.strip() if years_usage else None,
+                 num_projects.strip() if num_projects else None,
+                 category,
+                 now,
+                 now,
+             ))
+             conn.commit()
+             skill_id_int = cursor.lastrowid
+     
+     return RedirectResponse(url=f&quot;/admin/tech-skills/{skill_id_int}&quot;, status_code=303)

+ @app.get(&quot;/api/tech-skills&quot;)
+ def api_tech_skills() -&gt; JSONResponse:
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;API endpoint to fetch all tech skills for frontend&quot;&quot;&quot;
+     try:
+         with get_tech_skills_conn() as conn:
+             skills = conn.execute(&quot;&quot;&quot;
+                 SELECT 
+                     id,
+                     skill_name,
+                     logo_url,
+                     description,
+                     skill_level,
+                     years_usage,
+                     num_projects,
+                     category
+                 FROM tech_skills
+                 ORDER BY category, skill_name
+             &quot;&quot;&quot;).fetchall()
+         
+         # Group skills by category
+         result = {}
+         for skill in skills:
+             cat = skill[&quot;category&quot;]
+             if cat not in result:
+                 result[cat] = []
+             
+             result[cat].append({
+                 &quot;name&quot;: skill[&quot;skill_name&quot;],
+                 &quot;logo&quot;: skill[&quot;logo_url&quot;] or &quot;&quot;,
+                 &quot;level&quot;: skill[&quot;skill_level&quot;],
+                 &quot;years&quot;: skill[&quot;years_usage&quot;] or &quot;&quot;,
+                 &quot;projects&quot;: skill[&quot;num_projects&quot;] or &quot;&quot;,
+                 &quot;description&quot;: skill[&quot;description&quot;] or &quot;&quot;,
+             })
+         
+         return JSONResponse(content={&quot;skills&quot;: result})
+     except Exception as e:
+         return JSONResponse(content={&quot;skills&quot;: {}, &quot;error&quot;: str(e)}, status_code=500)
+ 
+
```

```diff
+         const tbody = document.getElementById(&#39;categories-list&#39;);
+         if (tbody) {
+             const sortable = Sortable.create(tbody, {
+                 handle: &#39;tr&#39;,
+                 animation: 150,
+                 onEnd: function(evt) {
+                     // Get all rows and their new order
+                     const rows = Array.from(tbody.querySelectorAll(&#39;tr[data-category-id]&#39;));
+                     const orders = {};
+                     rows.forEach((row, index) =&gt; {
+                         const categoryId = row.getAttribute(&#39;data-category-id&#39;);
+                         orders[categoryId] = index + 1;
+                     });
+                     
+                     // Update display_order in database
+                     fetch(&#39;/admin/tech-skills/categories/reorder&#39;, {
+                         method: &#39;POST&#39;,
+                         headers: {
+                             &#39;Content-Type&#39;: &#39;application/x-www-form-urlencoded&#39;,
+                         },
+                         body: &#39;category_orders=&#39; + encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify(orders))
+                     })
+                     .then(response =&gt; response.json())
+                     .then(data =&gt; {
+                         if (data.success) {
+                             // Update the order numbers in the table
+                             rows.forEach((row, index) =&gt; {
+                                 const orderCell = row.querySelector(&#39;td:first-child&#39;);
+                                 if (orderCell) {
+                                     orderCell.textContent = index + 1;
+                                 }
+                             });
+                         } else {
+                             alert(&#39;Error reordering categories: &#39; + (data.error || &#39;Unknown error&#39;));
+                             location.reload();
+                         }
+                     })
+                     .catch(error =&gt; {
+                         console.error(&#39;Error:&#39;, error);
+                         alert(&#39;Error reordering categories&#39;);
+                         location.reload();
+                     });
+                 }
+             });
+         }
+     });
+ &lt;/script&gt;
+ {% endblock %}
+
```

## Summary

Converted the hardcoded tabs to a dynamic, admin-managed category system.

### Database changes
1. Created `tech_skill_categories` table with:
   - `id`, `name` (unique), `display_order`, timestamps
   - Index on `display_order` for sorting
2. Updated `tech_skills` table:
   - Changed from `category` (TEXT) to `category_id` (INTEGER)
   - Added foreign key constraint

### Backend admin features
1. Category management routes:
   - `/admin/tech-skills/categories` — List all categories with skill counts
   - `/admin/tech-skills/categories/new` — Create new category
   - `/admin/tech-skills/categories/{id}` — Edit category
   - `/admin/tech-skills/categories/save` — Save category (create/update)
   - `/admin/tech-skills/categories/reorder` — Drag-and-drop reordering
   - `/admin/tech-skills/categories/{id}/delete` — Delete (only if no skills)

2. Auto-initialization: `ensure_tech_skills_categories()` populates default categories if none exist

3. Updated tech skills routes to use `category_id` instead of category name

### Admin templates
1. `tech_skill_categories_list.html`:
   - Shows all categories with order, name, and skill count
   - Drag-and-drop reordering (SortableJS)
   - Delete protection (can't delete if category has skills)

2. `tech_skill_category_edit.html`:
   - Form for name and display order
   - Auto-suggests next order number for new categories

3. Updated `tech_skill_edit.html`:
   - Category dropdown populated from database
   - Link to manage categories

4. Updated `tech_skills_list.html`:
   - Shows category name from joined table

### Frontend changes
1. Dynamic tab generation:
   - Tabs generated from API categories
   - Ordered by `display_order`
   - Tab keys generated from category names

2. API endpoint updated:
   - Returns `categories` array with order info
   - Skills grouped by category name

### Sidebar
- Added "Categories" link under "Experience / Skills" section

### Features
- Add new categories anytime
- Reorder categories via drag-and-drop
- Edit category names and order
- Delete empty categories
- Frontend automatically reflects changes
- Default categories auto-populated on first run

The system is now fully dynamic. You can manage categories from the admin panel, and the frontend will automatically display them in the order you specify.

```diff
+ #!/usr/bin/env python3
+ &quot;&quot;&quot;Migration script to update tech_skills database schema&quot;&quot;&quot;
+ import sqlite3
+ from pathlib import Path
+ from datetime import datetime
+ 
+ TECH_SKILLS_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / &quot;tech-skills&quot;
+ TECH_SKILLS_DB_PATH = TECH_SKILLS_DIR / &quot;tech-skills.sqlite&quot;
+ 
+ def migrate():
+     if not TECH_SKILLS_DB_PATH.exists():
+         print(&quot;Database does not exist, nothing to migrate&quot;)
+         return
+     
+     conn = sqlite3.connect(str(TECH_SKILLS_DB_PATH))
+     cursor = conn.cursor()
+     
+     try:
+         # Check if migration is needed
+         cursor.execute(&quot;PRAGMA table_info(tech_skills)&quot;)
+         columns = [col[1] for col in cursor.fetchall()]
+         
+         has_category_id = &#39;category_id&#39; in columns
+         has_category = &#39;category&#39; in columns
+         has_categories_table = cursor.execute(
+             &quot;SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type=&#39;table&#39; AND name=&#39;tech_skill_categories&#39;&quot;
+         ).fetchone() is not None
+         
+         if has_category_id and has_categories_table:
+             print(&quot;Database already migrated&quot;)
+             return
+         
+         print(&quot;Starting migration...&quot;)
+         
+         # Create categories table if it doesn&#39;t exist
+         if not has_categories_table:
+             print(&quot;Creating tech_skill_categories table...&quot;)
+             cursor.execute(&quot;&quot;&quot;
+                 CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tech_skill_categories (
+                   id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
+                   name            TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
+                   display_order   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
+                   created_at      TEXT DEFAULT (datetime(&#39;now&#39;)),
+                   updated_at      TEXT DEFAULT (datetime(&#39;now&#39;))
+                 )
+             &quot;&quot;&quot;)
+             cursor.execute(&quot;CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_categories_display_order ON tech_skill_categories(display_order)&quot;)
+         
+         # If we have old category column, migrate data
+         if has_category and not has_category_id:
+             print(&quot;Migrating category data...&quot;)
+             # Get unique categories from existing skills
+             cursor.execute(&quot;SELECT DISTINCT category FROM tech_skills WHERE category IS NOT NULL AND category != &#39;&#39;&quot;)
+             existing_categories = [row[0] for row in cursor.fetchall()]
+             print(f&quot;Found {len(existing_categories)} unique categories&quot;)
+             
+             # Create categories and map them
+             now = datetime.now().isoformat()
+             category_map = {}
+             order = 1
+             
+             for cat_name in existing_categories:
+                 if cat_name:
+                     # Check if category already exists
+                     cursor.execute(&quot;SELECT id FROM tech_skill_categories WHERE name = ?&quot;, (cat_name,))
+                     existing = cursor.fetchone()
+                     if existing:
+                         category_map[cat_name] = existing[0]
+                     else:
+                         cursor.execute(&quot;&quot;&quot;
+                             INSERT INTO tech_skill_categories (name, display_order, created_at, updated_at)
+                             VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
+                         &quot;&quot;&quot;, (cat_name, order, now, now))
+                         category_map[cat_name] = cursor.lastrowid
+                         print(f&quot;  Created category: {cat_name} (ID: {category_map[cat_name]})&quot;)
+                         order += 1
+             
+             # Add category_id column
+             print(&quot;Adding category_id column...&quot;)
+             cursor.execute(&quot;ALTER TABLE tech_skills ADD COLUMN category_id INTEGER&quot;)
+             
+             # Update category_id based on category name
+             print(&quot;Updating category_id for existing skills...&quot;)
+             for cat_name, cat_id in category_map.items():
+                 cursor.execute(&quot;UPDATE tech_skills SET category_id = ? WHERE category = ?&quot;, (cat_id, cat_name))
+                 updated = cursor.rowcount
+                 if updated &gt; 0:
+                     print(f&quot;  Updated {updated} skills to category_id {cat_id} ({cat_name})&quot;)
+             
+             # For any skills without a category, create a default one
+             cursor.execute(&quot;SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tech_skills WHERE category_id IS NULL&quot;)
+             null_count = cursor.fetchone()[0]
+             if null_count &gt; 0:
+                 print(f&quot;Found {null_count} skills without category, creating &#39;Uncategorized&#39;...&quot;)
+                 cursor.execute(&quot;SELECT id FROM tech_skill_categories WHERE name = &#39;Uncategorized&#39;&quot;)
+                 uncategorized = cursor.fetchone()
+                 if not uncategorized:
+                     cursor.execute(&quot;&quot;&quot;
+                         INSERT INTO tech_skill_categories (name, display_order, created_at, updated_at)
+                         VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
+                     &quot;&quot;&quot;, (&#39;Uncategorized&#39;, 9999, now, now))
+                     uncat_id = cursor.lastrowid
+                 else:
+                     uncat_id = uncategorized[0]
+                 cursor.execute(&quot;UPDATE tech_skills SET category_id = ? WHERE category_id IS NULL&quot;, (uncat_id,))
+                 print(f&quot;  Updated {null_count} skills to Uncategorized&quot;)
+             
+             # Create new table with correct schema
+             print(&quot;Creating new table with correct schema...&quot;)
+             cursor.execute(&quot;&quot;&quot;
+                 CREATE TABLE tech_skills_new (
+                   id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
+                   skill_name      TEXT NOT NULL,
+                   logo_url        TEXT,
+                   description     TEXT,
+                   skill_level     TEXT NOT NULL,
+                   years_usage     TEXT,
+                   num_projects    TEXT,
+                   category_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,
+                   created_at      TEXT DEFAULT (datetime(&#39;now&#39;)),
+                   updated_at      TEXT DEFAULT (datetime(&#39;now&#39;)),
+                   FOREIGN KEY (category_id) REFERENCES tech_skill_categories(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
+                 )
+             &quot;&quot;&quot;)
+             
+             # Copy data
+             print(&quot;Copying data to new table...&quot;)
+             cursor.execute(&quot;&quot;&quot;
+                 INSERT INTO tech_skills_new 
+                 (id, skill_name, logo_url, description, skill_level, years_usage, num_projects, category_id, created_at, updated_at)
+                 SELECT id, skill_name, logo_url, description, skill_level, years_usage, num_projects, category_id, created_at, updated_at
+                 FROM tech_skills
+             &quot;&quot;&quot;)
+             copied = cursor.rowcount
+             print(f&quot;  Copied {copied} skills&quot;)
+             
+             # Drop old table and rename new one
+             print(&quot;Replacing old table...&quot;)
+             cursor.execute(&quot;DROP TABLE tech_skills&quot;)
+             cursor.execute(&quot;ALTER TABLE tech_skills_new RENAME TO tech_skills&quot;)
+             
+             # Recreate indexes
+             print(&quot;Recreating indexes...&quot;)
+             cursor.execute(&quot;CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tech_skills_name ON tech_skills(skill_name)&quot;)
+             cursor.execute(&quot;CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tech_skills_category_id ON tech_skills(category_id)&quot;)
+             cursor.execute(&quot;CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tech_skills_level ON tech_skills(skill_level)&quot;)
+             cursor.execute(&quot;CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tech_skills_created_at ON tech_skills(created_at)&quot;)
+         
+         conn.commit()
+         print(&quot;Migration completed successfully!&quot;)
+         
+     except Exception as e:
+         conn.rollback()
+         print(f&quot;Migration failed: {e}&quot;)
+         import traceback
+         traceback.print_exc()
+         raise

+ 
+ if __name__ == &quot;__main__&quot;:
```

db_path = Path('tech-skills/tech-skills.sqlite')
if db_path.exists():
    conn = sqlite3.connect(str(db_path))
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    
    # Check if table exists
    cursor.execute(\"SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='tech_skill_categories'\")
    table_exists = cursor.fetchone()
    print(f'Table exists: {table_exists is not None}')
    
    if table_exists:
        # Try the exact query
        try:
            categories = cursor.execute('''
                SELECT 
                    id,
                    name,
                    display_order,
                    created_at,
                    updated_at,
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tech_skills WHERE category_id = tech_skill_categories.id) as skill_count
                FROM tech_skill_categories
                ORDER BY display_order, name
            ''').fetchall()
            print(f'Query successful, found {len(categories)} categories')
            if categories:
                print(f'First category: {dict(categories[0])}')
        except Exception as e:
            print(f'Query error: {e}')
            import traceback
            traceback.print_exc()
    
    conn.close()
else:
    print('Database does not exist')

```diff
+                     }
+                 });
+             }
+         },
+         totalPages() {
+             const total = this.categories.length;
+             return Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total / this.perPage));
+         },
+         paginatedCategories() {
+             const start = (this.currentPage - 1) * this.perPage;
+             return this.categories.slice(start, start + this.perPage);
+         },
+         goToPage(page) {
+             const total = this.totalPages();
+             this.currentPage = Math.min(Math.max(page, 1), total);
+         },
+         prevPage() {
+             this.goToPage(this.currentPage - 1);
+         },
+         nextPage() {
+             this.goToPage(this.currentPage + 1);
+         },
+         pageWindow() {
+             const total = this.totalPages();
+             if (total &lt;= 2) {
+                 return Array.from({ length: total }, (_, idx) =&gt; idx + 1);
+             }
+             const start = Math.max(1, Math.min(this.currentPage - 1, total - 1));
+             return [start, start + 1];
+         },
+         rangeSummary() {
+             if (!this.categories.length) {
+                 return &#39;Showing 0 items&#39;;
+             }
+             const start = (this.currentPage - 1) * this.perPage + 1;
+             const end = Math.min(start + this.perPage - 1, this.categories.length);
+             return &#96;Showing ${start}-${end} of ${this.categories.length} items&#96;;
+         },
+     };
+ }
  &lt;/script&gt;
  {% endblock %}
-
```

```diff
+ &lt;script&gt;
+ function skillsTable(initial) {
+     return {
+         perPageOptions: [10, 20, 30, 50, 100],
+         perPage: 10,
+         currentPage: 1,
+         skills: initial.skills || [],
+         init() {
+             this.$watch(&#39;perPage&#39;, () =&gt; { this.currentPage = 1; });
+         },
+         totalPages() {
+             const total = this.skills.length;
+             return Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total / this.perPage));
+         },
+         paginatedSkills() {
+             const start = (this.currentPage - 1) * this.perPage;
+             return this.skills.slice(start, start + this.perPage);
+         },
+         goToPage(page) {
+             const total = this.totalPages();
+             this.currentPage = Math.min(Math.max(page, 1), total);
+         },
+         prevPage() {
+             this.goToPage(this.currentPage - 1);
+         },
+         nextPage() {
+             this.goToPage(this.currentPage + 1);
+         },
+         pageWindow() {
+             const total = this.totalPages();
+             if (total &lt;= 2) {
+                 return Array.from({ length: total }, (_, idx) =&gt; idx + 1);
+             }
+             const start = Math.max(1, Math.min(this.currentPage - 1, total - 1));
+             return [start, start + 1];
+         },
+         rangeSummary() {
+             if (!this.skills.length) {
+                 return &#39;Showing 0 items&#39;;
+             }
+             const start = (this.currentPage - 1) * this.perPage + 1;
+             const end = Math.min(start + this.perPage - 1, this.skills.length);
+             return &#96;Showing ${start}-${end} of ${this.skills.length} items&#96;;
+         },
+     };
+ }
+ &lt;/script&gt;
  {% endblock %}
```

Updated the responsive breakpoints so columns hide in the specified order as the viewport shrinks:

## Column Hide Order:

1. **Logo/Icon** — `hidden sm:table-cell` — disappears first (< 640px)
2. **Description** — `hidden md:table-cell` — disappears second (< 768px)
3. **Category** — `hidden lg:table-cell` — disappears third (< 1024px)
4. **Projects** — `hidden xl:table-cell` — disappears last (< 1280px)

## Always Visible Columns:
- **Skill Name** (always visible)
- **Level** (always visible)
- **Years** (always visible)
- **Actions** (always visible)

On smaller screens, the category name appears under the skill name when the Category column is hidden (at the `lg` breakpoint and below). The table adapts to different screen sizes while keeping essential information visible.

Added filtering, sorting, and updated the pagination layout. Changes:

## Features Added:

### 1. **Filtering**
- Filter by Category: dropdown showing all categories that have skills
- Filter by Level: dropdown showing all skill levels present in your skills
- Filters work together (e.g., show all "Expert" skills in "Languages" category)

### 2. **Sorting**
- Sort by Skill Name (default)
- Sort by Category
- Sort by Level (ordered: Expert → Advanced → Medium → Learning → Beginner)

### 3. **Updated Pagination Layout**
- Bottom Left: Per Page dropdown (10, 20, 30, 50, 100)
- Middle: "Showing X-Y of Z items" summary
- Right Side:
  - "Prev" button (always visible, disabled on first page)
  - Page numbers: current page ± 2 pages (up to 5 numbers)
  - "Next" button (always visible, disabled on last page)

### Technical Details:
- All filtering and sorting happens client-side using Alpine.js
- Filters reset pagination to page 1 when changed
- Page numbers dynamically adjust based on current page and total pages
- Empty state shows "No skills match your filters" when filters exclude all results

The page now supports filtering, sorting, and pagination as requested.

Added a search input that filters skills by name as you type.

## Search functionality

1. **Search input field** — Added at the top of the filters section
   - Placeholder: "Type to search by skill name..."
   - Full-width, above the other filters

2. **Real-time filtering**
   - Filters as you type (1–2 characters)
   - Case-insensitive (e.g., "php" matches "PHP", "PHPUnit")
   - Partial matching (e.g., "jav" matches "JavaScript", "Java")

3. **Integration with other filters**
   - Works with Category and Level filters
   - Resets to page 1 when the search query changes
   - All filters work together

The search filters the skill name field and updates the results immediately as you type.

Fixed the Delete button. Changes:

## Fixes Applied:

1. **SortableJS configuration**:
   - Added `filter: 'a, button, form, input, select, textarea'` to prevent dragging when clicking interactive elements
   - This allows clicks on buttons/links without triggering drag

2. **Event handling**:
   - Added `@click.stop` to the Actions column and buttons to prevent event bubbling
   - Added `draggable="false"` to Edit and Delete buttons

3. **Delete button styling**:
   - Made it more visible with `font-medium underline`
   - Added `cursor-pointer` to indicate it's clickable

4. **Delete functionality**:
   - Added a `deleteCategory()` function that shows a confirmation dialog
   - After confirmation, it creates and submits the form programmatically
   - Shows the category name in the confirmation message

5. **Visual feedback**:
   - Disabled Delete text shows `cursor-not-allowed` and a tooltip when categories have skills

The Delete button should now be clickable and work with drag-and-drop. Clicking Delete shows a confirmation dialog, and after confirming, it submits the form to delete the category.

_**User (2025-11-13 02:31Z)**_

ok I get it, we cannot delete a category if there are existing skills attached to it.

---

_**Agent (model composer-1, mode Agent)**_



---


Yes, that's correct. This is intentional to maintain data integrity.

## Current behavior

- Categories with 0 skills: Delete button is enabled (red, clickable)
- Categories with 1+ skills: Delete button is disabled (gray, shows "Delete" with a tooltip)

This prevents:
- Orphaned skills (skills without a valid category)
- Breaking the foreign key relationship between `tech_skills` and `tech_skill_categories`
- Data inconsistencies

## If you need to delete a category with skills

1. Reassign the skills to another category (via the Skills Sets edit page)
2. Delete the skills first
3. Then delete the empty category

This keeps the database consistent and prevents errors. The system enforces this at the database level with a foreign key constraint (`ON DELETE RESTRICT`), so even if someone bypasses the UI, the database will prevent deletion.

If you want a different behavior (e.g., auto-reassign skills to a default category when deleting), I can implement that.
